newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says it consulting on Sierra Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says it consulting on Sierra Leone coup.

text.p: Military-ruled Nigeria, which has massed troops in Sierra Leone, said on Saturday it was consulting with other regional nations on the action to take over the coup in the small West African state.

"My head of state has been holding intensive sub-regional consultations at all levels and is taking appropriate action to ensure that quick restoration of peace, stability and legitimate government must take place in Sierra Leone," foreign minister Tom Ikimi told state radio in the first official Nigerian comment on the coup.
Ikimi was speaking from Harare, Zimbabwe, where he is attending preparatory meetings of the annual summit of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
The coup leaders say negotiations are under way in a bid to avert a possible attack by the Nigerian-led regional force to restore the ousted elected government of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
"We have always insisted that President Tejan Kabbah is a good leader, upright in stature, a gentleman and a man of peace," Ikimi said.

"But it is also important for us to recognise that the real circumstances in any country should be properly addressed before rushing for elections," he added in tacit defence of Nigeria's own long transition to democracy programme.
Kabbah was elected about a year ago, when Sierra Leone army was fighting a civil war with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF).
He signed a peace accord with RUF but skirmishes have continued and the rebels are now backing the coup leaders.
"Members of the international community who overdramatised the need for free elections in Sierra Leone are now mainly pre-occupied with evacuation of their citizens from that country," Ikimi said.
Last Sunday's coup by junior officers led by Major Johnny Paul Koromah has been roundly condemned internationally, with mounting calls for restoration of Kabbah, who fled to neighbouring Guinea.

Nigeria leads the West African ECOMOG regional peacekeeping force which was sent to Liberia in 1990. Some ECOMOG troops, including Nigerians, have been based in Sierra Leone while fresh troops have arrived to back them.
